📧 Email

An email from Laylo

📧👋
From: Laylo · To: Emma

Hello Emma! Thank you for your email from London. My name is Laylo. I am eleven years old. I am a student at School 15 in Samarkand. Samarkand is a beautiful city in Uzbekistan.

This is my best friend, Madina. She is in my class. She is very funny! Bobur is her brother. He is not in our class. He is twelve. Bobur and Madina are my neighbours.

Our English teacher is Mrs Karimova. She is very nice. Every day she says, “Good morning, class!” We say, “Good morning, Mrs Karimova!” English class is my favourite. I am happy in English class. It is not difficult.

In Uzbekistan, we say “Assalomu alaykum!” to say hello. We say “Xayr!” to say goodbye. What do you say in England? Are you a student too? Please write soon!

Bye for now, Laylo

🌐 Blog

Bobur’s Blog: My Family

👨‍👩‍👧‍👦🏠🐱
Posted by Bobur · Monday

Hi! I am Bobur and this is my blog. I am twelve and I live in Tashkent. Today my blog is about my family. My family is big. There are seven people in our flat!

This is my mother. Her name is Dilnoza. She is a doctor. My father’s name is Akmal. He is a taxi driver. He is very busy every day.

My big sister is Zarina. She is fifteen. Her cat is Paxta. It is white and very lazy! My little brother is Sardor. He is five. His toys are everywhere!

My grandparents live with us too. My grandmother’s name is Halima. Her plov is the best in Tashkent! My grandfather is Yusuf. His jokes are very funny.

Who is the funniest person in my family? It is Grandpa Yusuf! What about your family? Who is in it? Write in the comments!

Pen Friends Chat

💬🌍
Group chat · Madina, Yuki, Ali, Tom
MadinaHi everyone! Welcome to our new chat. I am Madina. I am eleven. I am from Uzbekistan, so I am Uzbek. My hometown is Bukhara. It is very old and beautiful. Where are you from?
YukiHello, Madina! I am Yuki. I am from Japan. I am Japanese. My hometown is Osaka. It is a big city. My school is near my home. Where is Bukhara? Is it near Tashkent?
MadinaNo, it isn’t. Bukhara is in the west of Uzbekistan. Tashkent is the capital. Ali, where are you? Are you in Tashkent?
AliHi, girls! I am Ali. I am Uzbek, but I am not in Uzbekistan now. I am in London with my family. London is the capital of England. It is very famous. My new friend Tom is here too.
TomHello! I am Tom. I am from England, so I am English. My favourite country is Uzbekistan. Ali’s photos of Samarkand are amazing! Where is the best plov? Is it in Bukhara?

📔 Diary

Laylo’s Diary

📔⏰🏫
Monday evening

Dear Diary, today is Monday. It is my busy day! I get up at seven o’clock. My school starts at eight o’clock. But today I am at school at ten past eight. I am late! Oh no!

My first lesson is Maths at eight o’clock. Our teacher is Mr Rustamov. He is nice, but Maths is difficult for me. At nine o’clock we have English. English is my favourite subject!

At ten o’clock we have a break. Madina and I eat apples and talk. Then we have Science and Art. Art is fun! School finishes at one o’clock.

On Tuesday I have Music and PE. On Sunday there is no school. On Sunday I visit my grandma in Urgut. Her house is near Samarkand.

Tomorrow I want to be on time! My alarm clock is ready. Good night, Diary! Laylo

📖 Story

The New Girl in 6B

👧🏫✨
A school story

It is Monday morning at School 21 in Tashkent. The teacher says, “Children, this is Madina. She is new. She is from Bukhara.” Madina is very tall. She has long, curly hair and big brown eyes. She is very shy.

Laylo is short. She has straight black hair and green eyes. She is very friendly. “Hi, Madina! Is your hair black or brown?” she asks. “It is dark brown,” Madina says, and she smiles.

At break, Bobur runs to the girls. Bobur is short and very funny. He has short red hair! “What color is your bag, Madina?” he asks. “It is blue,” she says. “My bag is blue too!” Bobur says.

After school, the three children eat plov at Laylo’s house. Laylo’s grandma is old, but she is very kind. Now Madina is not shy. She is happy. She has two new friends!

🎉 Poster

Bobur’s Birthday Party!

🎂🎉🎈
Party poster · Samarkand

Happy birthday, Bobur! How old is Bobur? He is twelve! His birthday is in May. It is on Saturday, May 15th. Come to his big party at the Bahor Café in Samarkand. The party starts at 4 o’clock.

What can you do at the party? Eat plov and a big chocolate cake. Listen to a small concert. Bobur’s sister, Madina, plays the doira. It is an Uzbek drum. Watch a funny magic show with Magic Ali!

Please bring a game or a book for Bobur. Don’t bring sweets. Bobur’s grandma makes sweets for the party!

More fun events this year: The school film day is on June 1st. The Navruz festival is in March, on the 21st. Bobur’s friend Laylo is eleven. Her birthday is on October 3rd. See you at the party!

A letter from Ali

✉️🛏️🐱
From: Ali · To: Laylo

Dear Laylo, How are you? We have a new flat in Tashkent, and I have a new room! It is small, but I love it. Here is my room.

My bed is next to the window. There is a blue blanket on it. My desk is near the bed. My computer is on the desk, and my school bag is under the desk. There is a big lamp between the bed and the desk.

My clothes are in the wardrobe. My cat, Momiq, sleeps on the wardrobe! There is a red Uzbek carpet on the floor. It is from Grandma. My books are on a shelf above the bed.

The kitchen is next to my room. Mom makes plov there every Friday. Come to Tashkent in the summer! Please bring your photos. And don’t forget your football!

Write soon! Love, Ali

My neighbourhood in Tashkent

🏘️🌳🍞
Kids’ News · Tashkent · by Bobur, 11

Hi! My name is Bobur. I am eleven, and I live in Tashkent. My neighbourhood is small, but it is great. There is a big park next to my house. There are old trees and a lake in it.

There is a playground in the park, too. My little sister Madina loves it. Opposite the park, there is a bakery. The bread there is hot and yummy. Every morning my dad buys two big non.

Near my school, there is a library. There are about five thousand books in it! I go there on Saturdays with my friend Ali. There isn’t a cinema in my neighbourhood. We go to the city centre for films.

How many shops are there? There are four shops and one hospital. On Sundays, my family takes the bus to Chorsu bazaar. There are lots of fruits, spices and colourful bowls there. I love my neighbourhood!

The Super Kid Quiz

🦸⭐📝
Fun Kids Magazine · Quiz by Madina

Hi! I’m Madina, and I’m twelve. I live in Khiva. I can swim very well, but I can’t sing! What can you do? Do my quiz! Count your “a” answers!

1. Can you swim? a) Yes, very well. b) No, I can’t. 2. Can you cook plov? a) Yes, I can. b) No, but I can make tea. 3. Can you sing a song in English? a) Yes, I can. b) No, I can’t.

4. Can you draw animals? a) Yes, I can draw cats and horses. b) Only a little. 5. Can you dance the lazgi? a) Yes, I can dance very well. b) No, I can’t. 6. Can you speak three languages? a) Yes, Uzbek, Russian and English! b) No, only two.

RESULTS. 5–6 “a” answers: Wow! You are a super kid. 3–4 “a” answers: Great! You can do many things. 0–2 “a” answers: That’s OK! Everyone can learn. Ask a friend to help you. My friend Ali can’t swim, but he can draw very well!

My trip to Samarkand

🕌✨📷
Laylo’s Travel Blog · Monday

Hello, friends! My name is Laylo, and I’m eleven. This summer, my family and I are in Samarkand. It’s a beautiful old city. You should visit it, too! Here is my advice.

First, you should go to the Registan. There are three big buildings with blue and gold tiles. Lots of tourists take photos there. In the evening, there is a light show. It’s amazing!

Next, you should go to Siyob bazaar. You should try the Samarkand non. It’s big, round and very tasty. My brother Bobur eats two every day!

Should you go in July? No, you shouldn’t! The weather is very hot then. You should go in spring or autumn. You should also see the Afrosiyob museum. There are very old wall paintings there.

What should you bring? You should bring a hat, water and a camera. Write a comment and tell me: Which city should I visit next?
